historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Defender 110 SVX - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the SVX (Special Vehicle eXperimental) launched in 1992, it brought premium, expedition-ready features to the iconic long-wheelbase Defender 110. Its engine lineage is rooted in Land Rover's legendary, robust 2.5-litre diesel units, evolving through the classic Tdi era into early electronic diesel management.

milestones.description: 200Tdi, 2.5L Diesel, 111hp (Introduction of the SVX special edition, featuring an upgraded interior, roof rack, and the proven, mechanically injected 200Tdi engine).
300Tdi, 2.5L Diesel, 111hp (Update to the 300Tdi engine, featuring improved refinement, the introduction of an EGR system, and the crucial steel locating dowel head gasket upgrade).
TD5 (10P/15P), 2.5L Diesel, 122hp (Later special edition and heritage continuation models adopted the electronic TD5, expanding the SVX legacy into the modern classic era).

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Land Rover Defender 110 SVX is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Land Rover Defender 110 SVX Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Land Rover Defender 110 SVX is a highly sought-after classic, and its 2.5-litre diesel engines are renowned for their durability. However, age and mileage can bring specific issues to the forefront. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: 300Tdi Head Gasket Failure - Why the Land Rover Defender 110 SVX 300Tdi Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Thermal stress and early plastic locating dowels allowing cylinder head movement, leading to gasket breach and coolant loss.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Stripping the top end, machining the head, and fitting upgraded steel locating dowels.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly effective for early symptoms; prevents recurrence if the block is undamaged.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the engine has suffered catastrophic overheating or block damage.

problems.recommendation: For early head gasket symptoms on a 300Tdi, a specialist repair with the upgraded steel locating dowels is highly effective and cost-efficient. However, if the engine has suffered catastrophic overheating or a seized TD5 ECU, a fully rebuilt unit with all known vulnerabilities addressed is the safest long-term choice for a vehicle of this caliber.

problems.h4: TD5 Injector Loom Oil Leak - Why the Land Rover Defender 110 SVX TD5 Loses ECU Function
problems.rootCause: Injector seals fail, allowing engine oil to track along the wiring loom directly into the Engine Control Unit (ECU), causing electrical failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing all injector seals and fitting a revised, sealed wiring loom.
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early before the ECU is permanently damaged.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if the ECU is destroyed or the engine has suffered secondary mechanical failure.
